newsitem.title: USA: U.S. appoints envoy on Bosnia war crimes - report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. appoints envoy on Bosnia war crimes - report.

text.p: The Clinton administration has appointed a special envoy for war crimes issues in an effort to shore up peace efforts in Bosnia after the scheduled departure of U.S. troops next year, the Washington Post reported on Wednesday.

The newspaper said David Scheffer, a close associate of Secretary of State Madeleine Albright who worked with her on war crimes issues while she was U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, had been nominated as ambassador-at-large.
But a State Department spokesman said he was unaware any such decision had been made and insisted there had been no announcement.

A total of 76 people have been indicted by an international tribunal based in The Hague, but none of the leaders who masterminded the war in the former Yugoslavia have been brought to justice. One trial has been completed and 67 of those indicted are still at large.
The State Department did announce on Tuesday that Albright will make her first trip to Bosnia as secretary of state later this month.
Spokesman Nicholas Burns said Albright's schedule was not yet firm but he added it would include a visit to Sarajevo the weekend of May 31 for talks with Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic.
